title: Commercial space reported vacant by a City landlord, grantee or payee
question: Did an organization the City pays tell the Tax Collector that a commercial space it owns or rents stood vacant, in years when the City was paying it?
finding: 578 vacancy reports are in the file for tax years 2022 to 2025. 4 spaces reported vacant belong to a filer that is a City landlord, grantee or payee on more than a name; 1 of them for two or more years. 333 Valencia Owner LLC (321-335 Valencia St, 2022, 2023, 2024; the City paid it $13.7 million in those fiscal years, mostly Public Health). Self-Help for the Elderly (933 Clement St, 2024; the City paid it $39.1 million in those fiscal years, mostly Human Services Agency). Abode Property Management (1174 Folsom St, 2024; the City paid it $4.7 million in those fiscal years, mostly Homelessness Services). 2339 Market I7 LP (2337-2339 Market St, 2023; the City paid it $25,770 in those fiscal years, mostly Mayor). 4 more rows are name matches only and are labelled so.
how: The Tax Collector publishes each Commercial Vacancy Tax filing for ground-floor space in the named neighborhood commercial districts: parcel, tax year, filer type, filer name, the filer's location number and whether the space was reported (or found) vacant, with the rate per foot of frontage. The location number is the registry's own location id, so each filing is tied exactly to a business registration; that registration's ownership and trade names are then compared with City payee names. A row is treated as more than a name match only when the organization is a profiled City-funded nonprofit or the payee is named for the address itself. "Paid in those fiscal years" covers the fiscal years that overlap the tax years shown.
limits: The tax covers street-level commercial space only, so a vacancy here is usually a shop front, not the offices or housing above it that the City may be paying for; the filing does not say which unit. A space can be vacant for repairs, a permit wait or a tenant search, and the tax has exemptions. The file covers the named districts only: most City-funded premises are outside it. 32 vacancy reports carry no location number and could not be tied to a registration. Filers that read as private individuals are not listed.
